# SSCCS Foundation (In Formation) {.unnumbered .unlisted}

## I. Establishment, Name, and Legal Status

1.  The entity hereby constituted shall be known as "SSCCS Foundation (in formation)".
2.  The Foundation is established as an independent, non-profit legal entity and shall acquire legal personality upon incorporation or registration in accordance with the laws of the jurisdiction in which such incorporation or registration is effected.
3.  The registered office of the Foundation shall be determined upon incorporation and may be transferred in accordance with applicable law.
4.  The Foundation is constituted exclusively for public-benefit purposes as set forth herein.

## II. Objects

1.  The objects of the Foundation are to promote and advance:
    a. science and research;
    b. education; and
    c. environmentally sustainable and energy-efficient technological development.

2.  In furtherance of these objects, the Foundation may, without limitation:
    a. conduct, support, and disseminate scientific research, including research relating to the Scheme-Segment Structure-based, Composition and Observation-driven Computing System (SSCCS) and related computational frameworks;
    b. develop, publish, and maintain open-source software and technical documentation;
    c. prepare and distribute academic publications, instructional materials, and research reports;
    d. facilitate cooperation and exchange among researchers, institutions, and organizations internationally;
    e. organize and support conferences, seminars, workshops, and related educational activities;
    f. establish and manage intellectual property rights, including copyrights and patents, in a manner consistent with the Foundation's non-profit and public-benefit purposes;
    g. adopt, utilize, and promote permissive open-source licenses for software developed by or contributed to the Foundation, including but not limited to the Apache 2.0 License, and shall hold or manage any associated copyrights or ownership interests to ensure the licensed software remains perpetually free and open;
    h. undertake such other lawful activities as are incidental or conducive to the attainment of the foregoing objects.

3.  The Foundation shall not carry on activities that are inconsistent with its non-profit character or public-benefit purpose.

## III. Non-Profit Character and Application of Assets

1.  The Foundation shall operate exclusively on a non-profit basis.
2.  The income and assets of the Foundation shall be applied solely toward the promotion of its objects as set forth in this Charter and Statute.
3.  No part of the income or assets of the Foundation shall be distributed, directly or indirectly, to any founder, governing body member, contributor, or private individual.
4.  The payment of reasonable remuneration for services actually rendered and the reimbursement of properly documented expenses shall not be deemed a distribution of profits.
5.  The Foundation shall not be organized or operated for the primary purpose of carrying on a trade or business for profit.

## IV. Governance

1.  The Foundation shall be governed by such bodies as are established upon incorporation in accordance with applicable law, including at minimum a governing body responsible for strategic oversight and an executive body responsible for management and representation.
2.  The composition, appointment, removal, powers, duties, and terms of office of members of such bodies shall be determined in accordance with applicable law and further specified in internal regulations or bylaws adopted pursuant thereto.
3.  All governing bodies shall exercise their functions in good faith, with due care, and in a manner consistent with the Foundation's objects and non-profit status.
4.  No governance arrangement shall authorize the diversion of the Foundation's assets from its stated objects.

## V. Financial Provisions

1.  The Foundation shall maintain accurate books and records of account and shall prepare financial statements in accordance with applicable law.
2.  Any surplus arising from the activities of the Foundation shall be retained and applied solely toward its objects.
3.  The Foundation may establish reserves or endowment funds to ensure its long-term sustainability, provided that such reserves are consistent with applicable law and the Foundation's non-profit character.
4.  The financial resources of the Foundation shall be managed with due diligence and prudence.

## VI. Dissolution and Asset Distribution

1.  The Foundation may be dissolved in accordance with applicable law.
2.  Upon dissolution, and after satisfaction of all lawful liabilities, the remaining assets of the Foundation shall be transferred to one or more organizations that:
    a. are organized and operated exclusively for public-benefit or non-profit purposes; and
    b. pursue objects substantially similar to those of the Foundation.
3.  In no event shall any remaining assets be distributed to private individuals or for private benefit.

## VII. Interpretation and Effect

1.  This Foundational Charter and Statute shall take effect upon the lawful incorporation or registration of the Foundation.
2.  The provisions of this document shall be interpreted so as to preserve, to the greatest extent permitted by applicable law, the non-profit and public-benefit character of the Foundation.
3.  If any provision is held invalid or unenforceable under applicable law, such invalidity shall not affect the remaining provisions, which shall remain in full force and effect.
4.  This document constitutes the foundational and governing instrument of the Foundation, subject to mandatory provisions of applicable law.
